title: Uzbek Cyrillic — ASCII passport style
description: Uzbek Cyrillic names to the ASCII form used in English and passport contexts: the official Latin spelling with oʻ→o, gʻ→g, tutuq dropped and Х→kh (Хўжаев → Khojayev, Мирзиёев → Mirziyoyev). Same output as uz_latin followed by uz_latn_ascii.
notes: No official Uzbek passport transliteration table was found (MIA rules for the biometric passport not retrieved). X→KH follows the Kun.uz (2022) report; Q is kept as Q. Status informal.

Do not use ICAO §6.B Ў→U for Uzbek: Ў is oʻ, so Ўринов → Orinov. The Soviet-legacy spelling Urinov (via Russian Уринов) is a variant to generate, as are Q→K, Gʻ→GH, J→DJ/DZH, H→KH, Ё→E, Ю/Я→IU/IA (Мирзиёев → MIRZIEEV under the Russian ICAO table).
Context rules as in uz_latin: Е→ye initially and after vowels/ъ/ь, Ц→ts after vowels otherwise s, ьи/ьо→yi/yo.

2026 reform: a law replacing Oʻ→Ö, Gʻ→Ğ, Sh→Ş, Ch→Ç (28 letters + apostrophe) passed the Legislative Chamber (July 2026) and the Senate (10 Sept 2026); presidential signature was unconfirmed as of 7 Oct 2026. Documents in the current alphabet stay valid; schools switch from 2027, textbooks by 2031. This scheme keeps the 1995 alphabet.
